label: prop:alpha-decay-gamow-tunneling
title: Zero-parameter Gamow--Gurney--Condon $\alpha$-decay tunneling and the $N=126$ shell-closure hindrance
html:
Heavy-nucleus \alpha-decay (Z, A) \to (Z - 2, A - 4) + {}^{4}\mathrm{He} tests simultaneously the derived fine-structure coupling, the nuclear contact length set by the pion Compton scale, and the vacuum behaviour of the q-exterior derivative outside a hadronic core. Following Hans Geiger and John Mitchell Nuttall (1911), George Gamow (1928) [gamow1928], and Ronald W. Gurney and Edward U. Condon (1928), an \alpha cluster separating from a daughter nucleus (Z_d, A_d) = (Z - 2, A - 4) releases exact inter-fragment proton-pair count

  \binom{Z}{2} - \binom{Z - 2}{2} - 1 = 2(Z - 2) = Z_\alpha Z_d

and tunnels from contact radius R_{\mathrm{touch}} to classical turning radius R_{\mathrm{turn}} = 2 Z_d \alpha_q \hbar c / Q_\alpha in exterior vacuum where the effective deformation relaxes to q_{\mathrm{local}}(r) \to 1.

With zero fitted nuclear parameters, all inputs are fixed by the three calibrations: the substrate parameter q_0 determines the Bring--Schwinger coupling \alpha_q^{-1} \approx 137.036, while the charged-pion Compton length r_\pi = \hbar c / m_{\pi^\pm} \approx 1.4138\;\mathrm{fm} fixes the tetrahedral bond \ell_{\mathrm{bond}} = \tfrac{3}{2} r_\pi and the face-centred cubic Wigner--Seitz radius constant

  r_0^{\mathrm{FCC}}
  = \left(\frac{3}{4\pi\sqrt{2}}\right)^{1/3}\frac{3}{2}\,\frac{\hbar c}{m_{\pi^\pm}}
  \approx 1.1721\;\mathrm{fm},
  \qquad
  R_{\mathrm{touch}} = r_0^{\mathrm{FCC}}\bigl(A_d^{1/3} + 4^{1/3}\bigr).

For reduced mass \mu and decay energy Q_\alpha = B(Z_d, N_d) + B_\alpha - B(Z, N) > 0 with x = R_{\mathrm{touch}} / R_{\mathrm{turn}} < 1, the sub-barrier WKB action and assault frequency \nu_0 = \sqrt{2 Q_\alpha / \mu}\,c / (2 R_{\mathrm{touch}}) determine the bare tunneling half-life

  2 G(Z_d, Q_\alpha)
  = \frac{2\sqrt{2\mu Q_\alpha}}{\hbar c}\,R_{\mathrm{turn}}
    \Bigl(\arccos\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x(1 - x)}\Bigr),
  \qquad
  T_{1/2}^{\mathrm{WKB}} = \frac{\ln 2}{\nu_0}\,e^{2 G(Z_d, Q_\alpha)},

recovering the affine Geiger--Nuttall scaling in Q_\alpha^{-1/2} at small x. If the core value q_0 > 1 persisted uniformly across the exterior Coulomb barrier (k_q = k / q_0), the exponent 2 G would shrink to 2 G / q_0, under-predicting the {}^{238}\mathrm{U} half-life by 3.42\;\mathrm{dex}; \alpha-decay therefore confirms directly that q_{\mathrm{local}}(r) \to 1 outside nuclear matter.

Open-shell benchmark versus the N = 126 shell closure

Evaluated at experimental AME2020 Q_\alpha values across heavy ground-state emitters spanning 24 orders of magnitude in observed half-life, the bare S_\alpha = 1 formula reproduces all five open-shell nuclei within 0.14--0.40\;\mathrm{dex} while isolating the classic closed-shell spectroscopic hindrance at magic N = 126 ({}^{210}\mathrm{Po}):

Nuclide N Q_\alpha (MeV) T_{1/2}^{\mathrm{exp}} T_{1/2}^{\mathrm{WKB}} \log_{10}(T^{\mathrm{WKB}}/T^{\mathrm{exp}}) S_\alpha^{\mathrm{emp}}
{}^{212}\mathrm{Po} 128 8.954 2.94 \times 10^{-7}\;\mathrm{s} 4.06 \times 10^{-7}\;\mathrm{s} +0.139 1.38
{}^{214}\mathrm{Po} 130 7.834 1.64 \times 10^{-4}\;\mathrm{s} 3.06 \times 10^{-4}\;\mathrm{s} +0.272 1.87
{}^{222}\mathrm{Rn} 136 5.590 3.30 \times 10^{5}\;\mathrm{s} 5.95 \times 10^{5}\;\mathrm{s} +0.256 1.80
{}^{226}\mathrm{Ra} 138 4.871 5.05 \times 10^{10}\;\mathrm{s} 1.10 \times 10^{11}\;\mathrm{s} +0.338 2.18
{}^{238}\mathrm{U} 146 4.270 1.41 \times 10^{17}\;\mathrm{s} 3.58 \times 10^{17}\;\mathrm{s} +0.405 2.54
{}^{210}\mathrm{Po} 126 5.408 1.20 \times 10^{7}\;\mathrm{s} 6.61 \times 10^{5}\;\mathrm{s} -1.257 0.0553

Two parameter-free mechanisms govern the observed preformation drop S_\alpha^{\mathrm{emp}}({}^{210}\mathrm{Po}) \approx 0.0553 across the N = 126 closure of Maria Goeppert Mayer (1949) [mayer1949] and Otto Haxel, J. Hans D. Jensen, and Hans E. Suess (1949):

  1. Mayer--Jensen seniority pair projection. Above N = 126, coherent pairing across the open valence shell enhances two-neutron transfer, whereas at closed N = 126 ({}^{210}_{84}\mathrm{Po}_{126} \to {}^{206}_{82}\mathrm{Pb}_{124} + \alpha) neutron superfluidity is quenched and the cluster draws two valence protons from 1h_{9/2}^2 (2 j_p + 1 = 10) together with two hole neutrons from 3p_{1/2}^{-2} (2 j_n + 1 = 2). The joint J = 0 single-subshell projection is
  S_{\mathrm{MJ}}^{(\pi \otimes \nu)}
  = \frac{1}{(2 j_p + 1)(2 j_n + 1)}
  = \frac{1}{10 \times 2}
  = 0.0500,

matching S_\alpha^{\mathrm{emp}} \approx 0.0553 to -0.044\;\mathrm{dex} and predicting T_{1/2}({}^{210}\mathrm{Po}) = T_{1/2}^{\mathrm{WKB}} / S_{\mathrm{MJ}}^{(\pi \otimes \nu)} \approx 1.32 \times 10^{7}\;\mathrm{s} (+0.044\;\mathrm{dex} from observation).

  1. Shell-kink chemical-potential barrier. By the derivative-discontinuity theorem of John P. Perdew, Robert G. Parr, Mel Levy, and Jose L. Balduz Jr. (1982), a shell closure is a convex-cone vertex kink where the two-neutron shadow price jumps by \Delta_{\mathrm{shell}}(126). Internal cluster formation across the pion-Compton range r_\pi = \hbar c / m_{\pi^\pm} carries WKB attenuation \exp(-2\sqrt{2\mu_\alpha\Delta_{\mathrm{shell}}}\,r_\pi / \hbar c). Using the categorical Compton oscillator spacing \hbar\omega_{\mathrm{QOU}}(210) = [m_e / (q_0 - 1)^2]\,210^{-1/3} \approx 7.11\;\mathrm{MeV} gives S_{\mathrm{kink}} \approx 0.0381 (-0.162\;\mathrm{dex}), whereas the empirical two-neutron separation jump S_{2n}(84,126) - S_{2n}(84,128) \approx 4.07\;\mathrm{MeV} gives S_{\mathrm{kink}} \approx 0.0845 (+0.184\;\mathrm{dex}), bracketing S_\alpha^{\mathrm{emp}} without free parameters.

Sensitivity to internally derived Q_\alpha

Replacing experimental mass differences by differences of the smooth face-centred cubic (k = 12, (111) surface deficit a_S / a_V = 3/4) standard-channel Borromean baryon binding Hamiltonian plus B_\alpha^{\mathrm{QOU}} = 64 m_e G \approx 29.96\;\mathrm{MeV} yields Q_\alpha^{\mathrm{FCC}}({}^{238}\mathrm{U}) \approx 3.966\;\mathrm{MeV} versus 4.270\;\mathrm{MeV} observed (\Delta Q_\alpha = -0.304\;\mathrm{MeV}). Because the Geiger--Nuttall slope reaches \partial\log_{10} T_{1/2} / \partial Q_\alpha \approx -8.52\;\mathrm{dex}/\mathrm{MeV} at {}^{238}\mathrm{U} (and -2.39 to -6.63\;\mathrm{dex}/\mathrm{MeV} across {}^{212}\mathrm{Po}--{}^{226}\mathrm{Ra}), that 0.30\;\mathrm{MeV} offset shifts T_{1/2}({}^{238}\mathrm{U}) by +3.15\;\mathrm{dex}, while omitting discrete shell-closure binding terms near N = 126 shifts Q_\alpha by several MeV and T_{1/2} by over 30\;\mathrm{dex}. Sub-dex half-life prediction from internal nuclear masses alone therefore requires \sim 0.05\;\mathrm{MeV} (30\;\mathrm{ppm}) shell-resolved binding accuracy.
